Hi Rishi,

Quick intro — I run product partnerships at NimbusWorks (Elena Park). We're evaluating options to embed an inference runtime into NimbusWorks Designer (our low-code automation UI) so customers can author automations with large-model actions without leaving the product.

High-level asks:
- Technical patterns: VPC/private deployment vs hosted API? What embedding options do you support for an ISV that ships a managed SaaS product?
- Licensing: up-front OEM fee vs per-customer metered billing vs revenue share — examples you have for ISV deals?
- Branding: can we white-label the service/SDK and what logo/attribution rules apply?
- Security: data residency, audit logs, SOC2 artifacts and optional on-prem packaging.

I've attached a short RFI that outlines our architecture and an initial set of questions. Looking to set up a 30-min call next week to walk through feasibility. Marcus (cc) is our Engineering lead.

Appreciate any initial pointers.

Elena — thanks for the RFI and the clear asks. Excited about the possibility — NimbusWorks' designer UX maps well to several ISV integrations we've done. Quick summary while I get our docs together and schedule a working call:

1) Deployment patterns
- Hosted (Redwood API): fastest to integrate, low friction for pilot customers, metered per-token pricing.
- Dedicated / OEM seats: reserved GPU pools we can dedicate to NimbusWorks tenants or a shared reserved pool with tenancy isolation. Works well when you need predictable throughput and lower unit cost.
- Private (VPC or on-prem): full private control plane for regulated customers; we provide an on-prem bundle if required.

2) Licensing models we've used with ISVs
- Annual OEM license + per-seat runtime usage tiering (common for embedded UI where you want fixed predictability).
- Revenue share for channel/reseller models (rare, used when partner handles customer billing).
- Pure pay-as-you-go for early pilots.

3) Branding & SDK
- We provide an SDK and an option for subdued co-branding. Full white-label (no Redwood mention) is available on enterprise contracts with governed support SLAs.

4) Security artifacts
- SOC 2 Type II report, penetration test summaries, and support for customer-specific questionnaires. VPC/private gives you stronger separation.

I've attached a short OEM terms doc (non-final) to frame commercial options and a copy of our standard OEM redlines we usually start with. Marissa (partnerships) will lead commercial conversations; Dev is looped for technical design.

If this looks good, can we schedule a 30–45m technical + commercial sync next Tue (10/26) or Wed (10/27)? I'll include a short mutual action plan on the call.

Cheers,

- Multi-tenant model: we'd prefer a shared runtime model in which NimbusWorks manages customer onboarding in our UI; can you confirm token isolation and per-tenant quotas when using Dedicated?

Hi Elena / Marcus — great to meet you both (virtually).

Quick follow-ups from our side ahead of the technical call on Wednesday:

- Commercial construct: We typically propose a two-phase approach for ISVs building embedded experiences:
  1) Pilot: hosted or shared dedicated capacity, short-term usage discounts, joint success metrics.
  2) Production/OEM: reserved Dedicated pool or Private deployment + annual OEM fee + volume tiers.

- Support & SLAs: OEM customers get 24/7 support, a named technical account lead, and 99.9% availability SLAs for Dedicated deployments.

- Ops playbook: we'll share an ops playbook that covers onboarding, per-tenant telemetry, incident runbooks, and rollout patterns (canary, tenant scoping).

Attached is a short ops checklist that we use for partner embed projects — it lists telemetry hooks and the minimal integration points for product teams. For the long-context ask Marcus mentioned, we'll have Dev walk through model/kv options on the call.

Looking forward to the call on Wed.

Warmly,
